items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: we knew about each other. Big Nick told me one night

ctx.x: From the Paradise Theatre, yeah. And they had a great, great band in there, a really good band, like some of the top players in the band... He really had started out the club with Kelly Martin, a fine drummer, and he had guys like Howard McGhee and a lot of great players who were in that band. But by the time I got there Howard was gone, but we knew about each other. Big Nick told me one night, he says, "Look, man," he says...

items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: And Big Nick Nicholas came when Lorenzo Lawson...when we replaced Lorenzo.

ctx.x: And we had some other guys that came through the band, like Matthew Gee, the trombonist -- he played with the band. And Big Nick Nicholas came when Lorenzo Lawson...when we replaced Lorenzo. And later on, when he left, they decided to use two altos and a tenor; then Wardell Gray came in playing the other alto saxophone.

And after the Jimmie Lunceford Orchestra broke up, Wardell had gone, and Ted Buckner, the famous alto saxophone player with Jimmie Lunceford; Detroit is his home, and so he came into the band. I was playing the lead alto, so I said, "Well, no, I'll have to give up the lead chair now." So he said, "No, don't give up the chair." He said, "I'll play third, and then I'll play some of the first. We'll split the book." Which was really nice, you know, because he was such a great player. In fact, a lot of the things…
